label: CP-0 arm distinctness -- arms with prompts that individually exceed the cap (cps 512 / 1024 / 2048)

dropped_restrictions.req_split_n_ge_min: withdrawn, not silently dropped. The 2nd audit (K3) showed the >=6 threshold was not a derivation: ceil(delta*N) equates a goodput RATIO with a request COUNT, and canon CONSENSUS §1-24 (stall probe: 16 of 17 stalls held by the probe's longest prompt) contradicts the equal-contribution premise the equation needs. CP-0 therefore excludes no arm at all -- all six boots are measured and the arm-set decision moves to the CP-1 pre-registration, which will be written against these measurements instead of the withdrawn threshold.

req_channel.why: served_population.json: 51 / 10 / 4 of the 200 served prompts individually exceed 512 / 1024 / 2048 tokens. A prompt longer than the cap cannot fit one budget even alone, so it is chunked regardless of backlog -- this makes req_channel=active OVER-DETERMINED and independent of the batch-budget mechanism (schedule_policy.py:802-842). 'unmeasured' stays live because the extraction itself can fail, which PROJECT_STATUS.md 'methodology gate' #21 requires be kept distinct from a finding. ★This why-string was rewritten on 2026-08-28: the earlier version leaned on prompt length as THE chunking mechanism, which is false (3rd audit F2, see RETRACTION_reqinactive_2026-08-28.md).

ARM_DISTINCT_BOTH.why: requires the batch cap to bind at EVERY probe rate including the lowest, i.e. even without backlog. Possible for cps 512 against a 341-token mean prompt, less so for 2048.

ARM_DISTINCT_REQUEST_ONLY.why: the request channel is over-determined for these arms (prompts individually exceeding the cap) while the batch cap may never bind at any registered probe rate.

ARM_DISTINCT_BOTH_RATE_DEPENDENT.why: the batch cap is expected to bind only once a backlog forms, so 'binds at the top probe rate but not the lowest' is the outcome the mechanism actually predicts. Registered ABOVE ARM_DISTINCT_BOTH because a cap that binds at every probe rate including the lowest would mean the arm is capped even without backlog.
